About the pictures. Every screenshot is from the real app, taken on made-up demo data (a simulated Nifty tape and sample trades), so the numbers are only examples and are not your results.

Nifty Paper Trader: how to use it

Paper money only. Nothing here places a real order. Not investment advice.

1. The screens

TabWhat it is for
StocksYour watchlist, the scanner ideas and today's strip. Tap a stock for its chart, order sheet and signal.
ScannerThe share scanner and the auto share trader: today's ideas, what was bought, and how each setup has done.
OptionsNifty and Sensex options: the live chart read, your auto trader, open trades and the log.
NewsThe morning news calls against what the stocks did.
TradesOpen positions, with live profit and loss.
AccountYour money, the rules (Limits, Entries), Research (studies, Combination Lab, Finder, saved data), Day review, the P&L charts and this guide.

2. A normal day

  1. Before 09:15: open the Options tab and check the auto trader is ON and your rules (Account > Limits and Entries) are what you want.
  2. During the day: you can leave it. Entries and exits are automatic.
  3. After 15:30: Account > Day review (every call against what happened), and Account > Research > Day report (copy it to paste in the chat).
  4. Once a week: run a study (section 5) and look at what paid and what did not.

3. How an options entry happens

  1. Every 15 seconds the app reads the Nifty (and Sensex) 1-minute candles and builds 5-minute bars.
  2. When a 5-minute bar closes, it checks your chart patterns and your combinations (Account > Entries). An entry is acted on only if the bar closed less than 4 minutes ago, and only once per bar.
  3. A signal becomes a trade only if the limits allow it:
  4. the entry hours (Account > Limits) and the trades-a-day cap are not used up
  5. the daily loss limit is not reached
  6. no call (or put) is already open
  7. 20 minutes have passed since a losing trade, and 15 minutes since a trade on the same side closed
  8. the stop is not wider than 2.5 ATR and one lot does not lose more than your loss limit at that stop
  9. the combination score (if you set a minimum) is high enough
  10. It buys one at-the-money contract for the weekly expiry, sized so the stop loses no more than your limit.

4. How an options trade ends

  • Chart stop: when a 1-minute candle of the index CLOSES beyond the stop level. One wick through the level does not count.
  • Profit ladder: once the profit reaches a row, the stop keeps that row's amount and then follows a fixed gap behind the best profit. A small gap sells on the first dip; a big gap gives back more.
  • Trail and break-even: optional, in points of the index.
  • Hard stop: a backup in the order engine for a fast gap.
  • 15:15: everything is closed.

5. Studies: what would have happened

A study replays past candles through your rules. It changes nothing live.

To run the Options study: Account > Research > Options study.

  1. Pick Nifty or Sensex.
  2. Pick the days. With real prices on, "10d" means the newest 10 days that have saved option prices.
  3. Keep "Use the real option prices" on. Without saved prices it falls back to an estimate and says so.
  4. Keep "Trade like the live bot" on, so the study obeys the same pauses, one call and one put at a time, the daily cap and the loss limit, and buys one minute after the signal bar.
  5. Pick trades a day (3, 5, 10 or your own setting) and the exit time.
  6. Press Run study.

Reading a row: net after charges, trades, win rate, average win and loss, the older half and the newer half, calls against puts, the hours, and "If a minimum chart score was needed".

  • Keep: made money on both halves. Unsteady: made money on one. Drop: lost. Too few: under 15 trades, so no verdict.
  • Older and newer half: a good result on both is worth much more than a big total made on one.
  • Score table: shows what a minimum chart score (40 to 80) would have done to that row. If 60+ keeps the profit and removes losers, set the Combination score to 60+.
  • Skipped by live rules: how many signals the pauses, the day cap, the holding rule and the loss limit removed. A study that skips a lot is telling you live will too.

Do not fool yourself.

  • 17 days is a short time. A combination chosen from 100 tried is partly lucky.
  • Paper-test a new combination for about two weeks before trusting it.
  • The study fills at candle prices. Real orders fill a little worse.

6. Making a combination

Account > Entries > My combinations > New combination.

  1. Name it.
  2. Pick checks (up to 20). Use search or the groups. Each check has a one-line description under its name. The dictionary at the end lists all of them.
  3. Rule: all together, or at least N of them.
  4. Event window: a "cross" or a "break" counts for this many bars (1 to 6, default 3).
  5. Index: Nifty, Sensex or both. Side: calls and puts, calls only, or puts only. A combination built from bullish checks should usually be calls only: its put twin is the mirror image and can buy puts on a rising day.
  6. Stop and exits: its own stop, ladder, trail and break-even, or the shared ones.
  7. Save, then test it in Account > Research > Combination Lab before you switch it on.

Good building rules

  • Use one entry check (a break or a cross) plus two or three filters (trend, breadth, time of day).
  • Add a filter only if the study shows it removes losers more than winners.
  • Do not stack ten checks. Few trades make any result unreliable.

A trend-day idea to test (not proven): Open drive + Breaks the opening range + Breadth 70%+ + ADX rising, calls only, entry hours 09:30 to 11:00.

7. Combination Lab, Finder and the View button

  • Combination Lab: one combination over 10, 15 or 30 days: every entry on a chart, day by day, and which extra check would have skipped each loser.
  • Finder: tries extra checks, pairs and triples, and judges them on older and newer days. Slower. A shortlist, not an answer.
  • View button: next to a trade in a study or the Lab. It opens a card that says why the entry happened (which checks held, and what each check means), what the index and the option did, how it ended, and the numbers.

8. Score

The chart score is out of 100 for a call and for a put, from about 15 signs (trends, EMAs, VWAP side, ADX, RSI, MACD, key levels, breadth, candle, and so on). A high score means many signs agree. It is not a promise. Patterns and combinations can have a minimum score (Account > Entries); it is off by default.

9. Profit and loss and the guide (Account)

  • P&L tile: your result with charts and tables: bars for each day, week or month, a running total, and tables by weekday, hour and symbol, for 7, 30 or 90 days or all. Shares and options are kept apart.
  • App guide: this file.

10. Honest limits

  • Studies are not live. The usual gaps: candle fills, late entries, sample size, and many combinations tried.
  • SEBI's study of FY25 found about 91% of individual F&O traders lost money (a total of about ₹1.05 lakh crore). Treat any option strategy as unproven until it survives weeks of paper trading.
  • A "big move day" cannot be predicted with one indicator. Several signs together (open drive, range break, wide breadth, rising ADX) raise the odds. They do not remove losing days.
  • Shares auto trading has done well on paper so far, but with few trades. Keep it on paper until it has weeks of results.

11. Dictionary of checks

A check is a state (it is true now) or an event (something just happened; it counts for the event window). A put uses the same check on the mirrored chart.

Trend

  • EMA 9 above EMA 21 (true now): The 9-bar average is above the 21-bar average: the short trend is up.
  • EMA 21 above EMA 50 (true now): The medium trend is up.
  • EMA 9 > 21 > 50 lined up (true now): All three averages are lined up upward: a clean trend.
  • Price above EMA 20 (true now): The last close is above its 20-bar average.
  • Price above EMA 50 (true now): The last close is above its 50-bar average.
  • Price above EMA 200 (true now): Above the long-run average (about 2.5 sessions of 5-minute bars).
  • Price above SMA 20 (true now): The last close is above the simple 20-bar average.
  • Price above SMA 50 (true now): The last close is above the simple 50-bar average.
  • Price above Hull average 21 (true now): The Hull average reacts faster than the others; price is above it.
  • EMA 21 rising (true now): The 21-bar average is higher than 3 bars ago.
  • EMA 50 rising (true now): The 50-bar average is higher than 5 bars ago.
  • Supertrend (10, 3) up (true now): The supertrend line is below price.
  • Supertrend (7, 2) up (true now): A quicker supertrend is below price.
  • Parabolic SAR below price (true now): The trailing dot sits under the price.
  • ADX over 20 and +DI over -DI (true now): A trend exists (ADX over 20) and buyers lead it.
  • ADX over 25 (strong trend) (true now): A strong trend is under way, either way. It does not pick a direction, so pair it with another check.
  • +DI above -DI (true now): Upward movement is stronger than downward movement.
  • Aroon up over 70 (true now): The high of the last 25 bars is recent and the low is old.
  • Aroon up above Aroon down (true now): The latest high is newer than the latest low.
  • Price above the Ichimoku cloud (true now): Price is above both cloud edges.
  • Ichimoku fast line above slow line (true now): The 9-bar midpoint is above the 26-bar midpoint.
  • Vortex +VI above -VI (true now): Upward vortex movement dominates.
  • Rising straight-line trend (20 bars) (true now): The best-fit line through 20 bars slopes up and fits well (R squared over 0.6).
  • Higher highs and higher lows (true now): The last 3 bars have a higher high and a higher low than the 3 before.
  • Above the day's open (true now): Price is above where the day opened.
  • Above yesterday's close (true now): The day is up.
  • Above yesterday's high (true now): Price is trading over the whole of yesterday.
  • Above the day's average price (true now): Price is above the average close of today so far.
  • Above the opening range (true now): Price is above the high of the first 15 minutes (after 09:30).
  • Near the day's high (true now): Within 0.3 ATR of the day's high.
  • TRIX above zero (true now): The triple-smoothed rate of change is positive.
  • Gapped up at the open (0.3%+) (true now): The day opened at least 0.3% over yesterday close.
  • Open drive (strong first half hour) (true now): After 09:30 price is at least 2 ATR over the open and never fell more than half an ATR under it: buyers took the day from the first bar.
  • Breaks the opening range (first 15 minutes) (just happened): The close crosses over the high of the first three bars for the first time.
  • Breaks yesterday's high (just happened): The close crosses over the whole of yesterday for the first time today.
  • 15-minute trend up (true now): The 15-minute averages (EMA 27 over EMA 63 on 5-minute bars) agree: the bigger picture is up, so a pullback is a gift and not a warning.
  • ADX rising (trend getting stronger) (true now): ADX is over 18 and higher than 3 bars ago, with buyers leading: a trend is building, not fading.
  • Market is trending (choppiness under 50) (true now): The choppiness index over 14 bars is under 50: price is travelling, not wandering. No direction by itself.
  • +DI crosses over -DI (ADX over 20) (just happened): Buyers take over the directional movement while a trend exists.
  • ADX over 25 and rising, buyers lead (true now): A strong trend that is still getting stronger, with +DI over -DI.

Momentum

  • RSI (14) above 50 (true now): Buying pressure leads.
  • RSI (14) between 50 and 70 (true now): Strong but not stretched.
  • RSI (7) above 55 (true now): A quicker RSI shows buying pressure.
  • RSI (14) rising (true now): RSI is higher than 3 bars ago.
  • RSI crosses up through 30 (just happened): The oversold bounce.
  • RSI crosses up through 50 (just happened): Momentum turns up.
  • MACD above its signal line (true now): MACD line over its 9-bar average.
  • MACD histogram positive and rising (true now): Momentum is up and growing.
  • MACD above zero (true now): The 12 EMA is over the 26 EMA.
  • MACD crosses above its signal (just happened): A fresh upward cross.
  • MACD histogram turns up (just happened): The histogram stops falling and rises while it is still below zero.
  • Stochastic %K above %D (true now): The fast line is over the slow line.
  • Stochastic %K above 50 (true now): Price is in the upper half of its 14-bar range.
  • Stochastic turns up from below 20 (just happened): %K crosses over %D while still under 20.
  • CCI (20) above 0 (true now): Price is over its typical level.
  • CCI (20) above 100 (true now): Unusually strong.
  • CCI crosses up through -100 (just happened): Bounce from an oversold reading.
  • Williams %R above -50 (true now): Price is in the upper half of its 14-bar range.
  • Williams %R crosses up through -80 (just happened): Leaves the oversold zone.
  • Awesome oscillator above 0 (true now): 5-bar midpoint average over the 34-bar one.
  • Awesome oscillator turns up (just happened): It rises after two falling bars.
  • Ultimate oscillator above 50 (true now): Momentum over three time frames is positive.
  • Price up over 10 bars (true now): The close is above the close 10 bars ago.
  • Pushed 1.5 ATR in 6 bars (true now): A fast move up.
  • Three higher closes in a row (true now): Steady buying.
  • RSI (2) dip bought in an uptrend (just happened): Connors style: the 2-bar RSI was under 10 and turns back over it while price is over the 50 EMA. A short dip in a rising market.
  • RSI (2) under 10 (true now): A very short-term oversold reading. On its own it fights the move; pair it with a trend check.

Volatility

  • Price above the Bollinger middle (true now): Over the 20-bar average, inside the bands.
  • Close above the upper Bollinger band (true now): A push beyond two standard deviations.
  • Price crosses up through the Bollinger middle (just happened): A fresh move over the average.
  • Bounce off the lower Bollinger band (just happened): Price dipped under the lower band and closed back over it.
  • Bollinger squeeze (tight bands) (true now): The bands are as narrow as at any time in the last 50 bars: a big move is brewing, either way.
  • Close above the upper Keltner channel (true now): A push beyond 1.5 ATR over the 20 EMA.
  • ATR expanding (true now): Ranges are 10% wider than 10 bars ago: the market is waking up. No direction by itself.
  • 20-bar high broken (just happened): The close is above the highest high of the 20 bars before.
  • Big bullish bar (true now): A bar of 1.2 ATR or more that closes in its top third.
  • Squeeze fires up (Bollinger leaves Keltner) (just happened): The Bollinger bands were inside the Keltner channel (a coiled market) and have just opened with price above the middle.
  • Narrow bar, then a wide bullish bar (just happened): The previous bar was the narrowest of the last 7, and this bar is wider and closes up over its high: quiet turns to movement.
  • Room left in the day (range under 80% of usual) (true now): Today's range so far is under 80% of the average of the last 5 days: the move is not used up yet. No direction by itself.
  • Bollinger squeeze, then a close above the upper band (just happened): The bands were the narrowest of the last 50 bars within the last 6 bars, and price now closes over the upper band.
  • 55-bar high broken (about 4.5 hours) (true now): The close beats the highest high of the 55 bars before: the turtle-style breakout.

Volume and VWAP

  • Price above VWAP (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Over the volume-weighted average of the day: buyers hold the day.
  • Price crosses up through VWAP (just happened, needs volume of the 50 stocks): A fresh move over the day average price.
  • VWAP rising (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): The day average is higher than 3 bars ago.
  • Price 0.5 ATR or more above VWAP (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Clear of the day average: the move has room, though it may be stretched.
  • Volume 1.5 times the usual (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Traded value is 1.5 times the average of the last 20 bars. No direction by itself.
  • Volume 2.5 times the usual (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): A surge in traded value. No direction by itself.
  • Heavy buying bar (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): A bullish bar on 1.5 times the usual volume.
  • OBV above its 20-bar average (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): On-balance volume trends up.
  • Chaikin money flow above 0 (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Bars close nearer their highs on volume.
  • Chaikin money flow above 0.1 (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Clear accumulation.
  • Money flow index above 50 (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Volume-weighted RSI shows more buying than selling.
  • Force index above 0 (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Price change times volume is positive.
  • Pullback on fading volume (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Price is lower than 3 bars ago but volume is under average: sellers are not pushing.
  • Pullback to VWAP that holds (just happened, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Price dipped to within 0.3 ATR of VWAP in the last 3 bars, closed back above it, and VWAP is rising: buyers defend the day average.
  • Quiet bars, then a break on volume (just happened, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Three bars on below-average volume, then a close over the 6-bar high on 1.5 times the usual volume: a coil that opens with money behind it.
  • Price over VWAP + 1 standard deviation (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Holding over the first VWAP band: a trend day reading.
  • Back inside from under VWAP - 2 standard deviations (just happened, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Price was under the lower 2-deviation band and closes back over it: a stretched fall snapping back.
  • Above the 2-day anchored VWAP (true now, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Price is over the VWAP anchored at yesterday's open: buyers of the last two days are in profit.
  • Money flow index crosses up through 50 (just happened, needs volume of the 50 stocks): The volume-weighted RSI turns to buying.

Pivots and levels

  • Price above today's pivot (true now): The close is over the floor pivot, (yesterday's high + low + close) / 3: the day leans to buyers.
  • Price above the CPR (true now): The close is over the whole central pivot range (the pivot and the middle of yesterday's high and low).
  • First close above the CPR today (just happened): Price opened at or under the CPR and has just closed over it for the first time today.
  • Narrow CPR day (true now): Today's CPR is under 60% of its average width over the last 5 days. Indian traders read a narrow CPR as a likely trending day. No direction by itself.
  • Wide CPR day (true now): Today's CPR is over 1.5 times its 5-day average width: usually a sideways day, better for fades than breakouts. No direction by itself.
  • Today's CPR above yesterday's (true now): The whole of today's CPR sits over yesterday's: value is moving up (an ascending CPR).
  • Pullback to the pivot that holds (just happened): Price dipped to within 0.3 ATR of the pivot (or the CPR top) in the last 3 bars and a bullish bar closes back over it.
  • First close above R1 today (just happened): Price breaks the first resistance, 2 x pivot - yesterday's low: a strong day.
  • Price above R1 (true now): Trading over the first floor resistance.
  • Breaks the Camarilla H4 (just happened): First close of the day over H4 (yesterday's close + 1.1 x range / 2): Camarilla traders treat it as a breakout and a possible trend day.
  • Reclaims the Camarilla L3 (just happened): On a day that opened inside H3 and L3, price closes back over L3 after being under it: the range-day fade.
  • Inside the Camarilla H3 to L3 (true now): Price is between H3 and L3: a balanced, range-bound reading. No direction by itself.
  • Above yesterday's value area (true now): Price is over the top of where yesterday spent 70% of its time (market profile, by time at price): buyers accept higher prices.
  • Above yesterday's busiest price (true now): Price is over yesterday's point of control, the price it spent most time at.
  • Back into value from below (80% rule) (just happened): The day opened under yesterday's value area and has now closed inside it twice in a row: price often crosses the whole area.
  • Opened inside yesterday's range (true now): Today opened between yesterday's high and low: no gap, so levels matter more. No direction by itself.

Candles

  • Bar closes up (true now): The close is above the open.
  • Close above the previous high (just happened): The bar closes over the previous bar high.
  • Closes in the top third (true now): Buyers won the bar.
  • Bullish engulfing (just happened): A bullish body that covers the previous bearish one.
  • Hammer (just happened): A long lower wick (twice the body, over half the range) and a close in the top third.
  • Three advancing bars (just happened): Three bullish bars, each closing higher with a real body.
  • Higher low formed (true now): The last bar low is above the low of the 5 bars before.
  • Full-bodied bullish bar (true now): A bullish bar with almost no wicks (body over 80% of the range).
  • Gap-and-go bar (just happened): A bar opening over the previous high and closing higher.
  • Heikin-Ashi: two strong green bars (true now): The last two Heikin-Ashi candles are green with no lower wick: a smooth push up.
  • Heikin-Ashi turns green (just happened): The first green Heikin-Ashi candle after two red ones.

Market

  • Nifty 50 breadth 60%+ (true now, needs breadth): At least 60% of the 50 stocks are above yesterday close (for a put: below).
  • Nifty 50 breadth 70%+ (true now, needs breadth): At least 70% of the 50 stocks agree.
  • Nifty 50 breadth 80%+ (true now, needs breadth): At least 80% of the 50 stocks agree: a one-way day.
  • Breadth improving (true now, needs breadth): The share of stocks on this side is 5 points higher than 3 bars ago.
  • Breadth crosses to the majority (just happened, needs breadth): More than half of the 50 stocks switch to this side.

Time of day

  • Morning (09:30 to 11:30) (true now): The most active hours.
  • Midday (11:30 to 13:30) (true now): The usual lull: moves are smaller and break less often.
  • Afternoon (13:30 to 15:00) (true now): Positions are built for the close.
  • After 10:00 (true now): Skips the opening noise.
  • Not midday (skips 11:30 to 13:30) (true now): Real-price tests found the midday lull wins least often. Use it as a filter beside an entry check.
  • First hour after the open (09:30 to 10:30) (true now): The hour most big one-way days are decided.

Chart patterns

  • Double bottom / top (just happened): Price makes the same low twice, with a bounce of at least 1.5 ATR between them, then closes above the bounce high. Stop under the two lows.
  • Double bottom / top, tighter stop (just happened): The same double bottom, but the stop sits half way between the lows and the neckline, so it fits the loss limit. It gives up the room under the lows.
  • Sharp fall, then turn (just happened): A fall of 4 ATR or more, then price turns off the low: a higher low and a bar that closes above the previous bar high, within 2 ATR of the low. Stop under the low.
  • Breakout of the last hour (just happened): A 5-minute bar closes above the highest high of the last hour (12 bars). Stop under the lowest low of the last 6 bars.
  • Opening range breakout (just happened): The first close beyond the 09:15-09:30 range after 09:30. Stop at the other end of that range.
  • Pullback in a trend (just happened): The 9, 21 and 50 EMAs are lined up, price dips to the 21 EMA and then closes above the previous bar high. Stop under the dip.
  • Engulfing candle at a low / high (just happened): After a few falling bars near the 20-bar low, a bullish candle whose body covers the previous bearish one. Stop under both.
  • Hammer / shooting star (just happened): A candle near the 20-bar low with a long lower wick (twice its body, over half the range) that closes in its top third. Stop under the wick.
  • Inside bar breakout (just happened): A big bar (1.2 ATR or more), a small bar inside it, then a close beyond the big bar. Stop at the big bar other end.
  • Supertrend flip (just happened): The supertrend (10, 3) turns from down to up. Stop at the supertrend line.
  • EMA 9 / 21 cross (just happened): The 9 EMA crosses above the 21 EMA with price above both. Stop under the last 6 bars.
  • Nifty 50 breadth (just happened, needs breadth): At least 70% of the 50 stocks are above (call) or below (put) yesterday close and the index is on the same side of its day average. Stop under the last 6 bars.
  • Opening range breakout (30 min) (just happened): The first close beyond the 09:15-09:45 range after 09:45, a wider and slower cousin of the 15-minute range. Stop at the other end of the range.
  • Yesterday's high / low break (just happened): The first 5-minute close of the day beyond the previous day's high (call) or low (put), after 09:30. Stop under the last 6 bars.
  • Strong momentum bar (just happened): A big bar (1.5 ATR or more) that closes in its top 15% and above the highest high of the last 6 bars. Stop under the bar.
  • VWAP reclaim / rejection (just happened, needs volume of the 50 stocks): Price closed under the volume-weighted average for 3 bars, then closes back above it on 1.2 times the usual volume. Stop under the last 6 bars. The index has no volume of its own, so VWAP and volume are built from the traded value of the 50 stocks.
  • VWAP pullback in a trend (just happened, needs volume of the 50 stocks): The index has held above a rising VWAP (8 of the last 12 bars), dips to touch it and closes above the previous bar high. Stop under the dip.
  • Breakout on high volume (just happened, needs volume of the 50 stocks): The breakout of the last hour, on at least 1.5 times the usual volume (traded value of the 50 stocks). Stop under the last 6 bars.
  • CPR breakout (just happened): The first close of the day above the central pivot range (yesterday's pivot and the mid of its high and low), on a day that opened under it. Traders watch it most on a narrow-CPR day. Stop under the last 6 bars.
  • Camarilla H4 / L4 breakout (just happened): The first close of the day beyond the Camarilla H4 (call) or L4 (put), yesterday's close plus half of its range times 1.1: often the start of a trend day. Stop under H3 or the last 6 bars, whichever is nearer.
  • Camarilla L3 / H3 reversal (just happened): On a day that opened inside H3 and L3, price dips under L3 and a bullish bar closes back over it (for a put: pokes over H3 and closes back under). A range-day fade. Stop under the last 6 bars.
  • Back into value (80% rule) (just happened): The day opened under yesterday's value area (where it spent 70% of its time) and then closes back inside it twice in a row: price often travels across the whole area. Stop under the last 6 bars.
  • Volume climax at a low / high (just happened, needs volume of the 50 stocks): A bar at the 20-bar low on 2.5 times the usual volume that closes in its top half: sellers look exhausted. Stop under the bar.

News

  • News points the same way (true now, needs news): A recent headline favours this trade and the price has not sold it off.
